major.name: Earth Science - BS - Geology Emphasis

requirement.description: 54-55 UD units are required, distributed as follows:
requirement.notes:
Recommended Electives: Earth 100, 111, 117 or 137, 123 or 159, 124AA-ZZ, 126, 157 or 186, 158, 176.
Preparation for Geohydrology:
Students interested in careers in geohydrology are recommended to take Earth 168 or 169 and Earth 173. Also recommended: Earth 113, 117, 125, 176, and Environmental studies 144.

narrative: An initial consultation with a departmental advisor is essential before embarking on the Earth Science major.

MAJOR REGULATIONSPREREQUISITES Check the General Catalog for the prerequisites to all listed courses.
P/NP GRADING OPTION Not allowed for any major course (Prep or UD major), including courses applied to the major from other departments.
SUBSTITUTIONS In the major requirements permissible only by petition to the department chair and dean.
G.P.A. REQUIREMENTS At least 2.0 overall UC average in all upper-division major courses and all courses (Prep and UD) for the major.
DOUBLE MAJORS With approval of each department, up to 8 units may be applied simultaneously to both UD majors.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Chemistry Courses
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory).

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Chemistry Courses
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Chemistry Courses
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1A. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent Mathematics 3A course.

nodes.title: General Chemistry Lab (Part A)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Chemistry Courses
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-. Concurrent enrollment, or a grade of C- or higher in CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B.
nodes.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop laboratory techniques and demonstrate the basic concepts of stoichiometry, gas laws, atomic spectroscopy, chemical equilibrium, and acid-base chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 2A or CHEM 1A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Thermodynamics (first and second law), electrochemistry, chemical kinetics, atomic and molecular structure, and chemical bonding.

nodes.title: General Chemistry Laboratory (Part B)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Chemistry Courses
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-. Concurrent enrollment, or a grade of C- or higher in CHEM 1C, CHEM 2C, or CHEM 3C. CHEM 2AL (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop laboratory techniques and demonstrate the basic concepts of buffers, thermochemistry, electrochemistry, kinetics, and colligative properties.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 2B or CHEM 1B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Structure and dynamics of the elements and their compounds. Aspects of technology and environmental problems.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: None
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory). First quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry. Second quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry. Third quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: Principles of Physical Geology
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division Earth Science Courses
nodes.description: Introduction to the science of the Earth; properties and processes of its surface and interior, including plate tectonics, volcanism, earthquakes, glaciation, mountain building, formation of rocks, minerals, and the structural basis of landforms. Lab and lecture each offering. There can be an additional 1 day local field trip.

nodes.title: Principles of Historical Geology
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division Earth Science Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 2 or 4 or 7 or 20.
nodes.description: Antiquity and history of the Earth from an Earth system history approach. Focus is on processes and changes over time of the Earth's lithosphere, biosphere, atmosphere, and hydrosphere.

nodes.title: Introduction to Oceanography
nodes.description: An introduction to oceanography covering the major physical, chemical, and geological features of the oceans, their role in Earth history, and potential use as a natural resource. Lab and lecture.

nodes.title: Dinosaurs
nodes.description: The origin and diversification of dinosaurs, including birds. Survey of evolutionary relationships within the group, and between the major groups of vertebrates. Broad introduction including anatomy, geography, climate, and vertebrate contemporaries.

nodes.title: Geological Catastrophes
nodes.description: Course deals with geologic catastrophes, e.g., earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis, and landslides. Students will learn the basic physical causes of these naturally occurring events and discuss the consequences.

nodes.title: Geoscience Communication
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division Earth Science Courses
nodes.description: Introduction to written and verbal communication skills in the Earth Sciences. Students attend the weekly department colloquium or other Earth Science related presentations, and read and discuss related articles. Weekly assignments develop scientific writing skills.

nodes.title: Petrology of Igneous Rocks
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 114 and 115 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the occurrence, associations, tectonics, and petrogenesis of plutonic and volcanic rocks. Introduction to the physical chemistry of magma systems; magmatic crystallization and differentiation; pluton emplacement, volcanic eruption mechanisms. Lab and lecture each offering. There can be an additional 1 day local field trip.

nodes.title: Metamorphic Petrology
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 114 and 115 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Study of metamorphic rocks to understand tectonic processes. Metamorphic minerals, metamorphic textures, physical processes responsible for metamorphism, phase equilibria, thermodynamics, diffusion, thermobarometry, kinetics, geochronology, and high-temperature rock deformation. Lecture and lab.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Structural Geology
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 104A or Earth 104G, and Earth 114 with a grade of C or better; Math 2B or 3B (may be taken concurrently); Physics 6A or 1 or 7A
nodes.description: Deformation of rocks--faulting, folding and flow. Theory and observations at scales ranging from mountain belts to microscopic. Lab, lecture and field trip(s). The field component consists of 1-2 one day trips and an overnight trip lasting 3-4 days.

nodes.title: Field Studies in Geological Methods
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 2; consent of department.
nodes.description: Introduction to the methods of geological observations and interpretations, with an emphasis on understanding earth processes in the field and reconstructing the physical history of the earth; the stratigraphic, petrologic, and structural relations of rocks. Lecture, lab and field trips. The field trip portion consists of 6–8 one day trips and commonly an overnight trip lasting 3-4 days.

nodes.title: Field Methods
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 114 and 103. All with a C- or better.
nodes.description: Geologic mapping on topographic maps and aerial photographs; use of geologic field instruments; field techniques; preparation of geologic maps and reports. Field work is completed during the break and between winter and spring quarters and consists of a 8-10 day overnight field trip.

nodes.title: Digital Analysis and Interpretation of Field Data
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 2
nodes.description: Introduction to commonly used computer programs and techniques for analyzing and visualizing surface and subsurface spatial and structural data in the Earth Sciences. Local site visits involve hands-on demonstrations in geologic data collection. Introduction to scientific writing. Lecture and Lab. This course includes 2–3 local afternoon field trips.

nodes.title: Earths Climate: Past and Present
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 2 or 3 or 4.
nodes.description: Description and quantitative analysis of climate processes and paleoclimate proxies. Processes include radiation and the Earths energy budget, the influence of orbital cycles, ocean circulation, monsoons, ENSO, and ice sheets. Paleoclimate reconstructions from tectonic-scale to the last millennium, with emphasis on glacial cycles and Plio-Pleistocene climate evolution.

nodes.title: Geomaterials
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 2
nodes.description: Examination of geomaterials at atomic level. Atomic structure, states of matter, bonding, elementary phase equilibria. Composition and structure of atmosphere, hydrosphere, crust, mantle and core. Structure and composition of important geochemical compounds emphasizing rock-forming minerals.

nodes.title: Analytical Methods in Geomaterials
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 114 with a grade of C or better
nodes.description: Optical properties of inorganic crystals; techniques of mineral identification using the polarizing microscope; strategies for studying rocks in thin section. Fundamental theory and application of electron and ion-beam instruments in quantitative characterization of geomaterials. Laboratory sessions include lectures as appropriate. Some offerings include a one day field trip.

nodes.title: Summer Field Geology
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 104A or 104G; and Earth 103, 104B, and 122. All prerequisites require a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Intensive hands-on training in the collection, interpretation, and presentation of geologic field data. Preparation of geologic maps, sections, and a professional report as tools to understanding geologic processes. Area and focus of investigation changes each year. This is a 6 week field course out of the Santa Barbara area.

nodes.title: Sedimentation and Stratigraphy: Processes and Products
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 2; and Earth 104A; and Earth 114. Field trip required.
nodes.description: Transport/depositional processes, sedimentary textures and structures. Sedimentary environments, using facies models for observation & prediction. Principles of lithostratigraphy, biostratigraphy, chronostratigraphy, and magnetostratigraphy. Seismic stratigraphy and sequence stratigraphic principles. Controls of tectonics, sediment supply and eustacy on sedimentation. Lab, lecture and field trip(s). The field component consists of some 1 day field trips and may include a 2-4 day overnight trip.

nodes.title: Introduction to Geological and Geophysical Data Analysis
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A.
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B; and Mathematics 4A-B.
nodes.description: Various numerical methods for analysis of data are developed. Methods are statistical inference, error propagation, least squares, time series as applied to geological and geophysical examples. Lab and lecture.

nodes.title: Ore Deposits and Mineral Resources
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 2; Earth 114 and 115
nodes.description: Distribution and characteristics of major classes of mineral deposits - their geologic framework, mineralogy, and structure. Lectures explore petrogenetic models for ore-formation. Laboratory exercises and field trips stress recognition of ore and accessory minerals, zoning, and exploration strategies. The field trip ranges from 1-4 days long.

nodes.title: Physical Volcanology
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.
nodes.prereq_text: Earth 104A, 114, and 115 (or Instructor Approval).
nodes.description: Overview of volcanic processes, including physical properties of melts, eruptive mechanisms, classification of volcanic deposits, and volcanic- tectonic environments. Lecture emphasizes theoretical aspects of volcanic processes, lab examines major classes of volcanic rocks, field trips emphasize mapping in volcanic terrains. Typically includes one to two overnight trips of 2-4 days each.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.

nodes.title: Differential Equations
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.

nodes.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
nodes.description: Introduction to differential and integral calculus with applications to modeling in the biological sciences.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Introduction to classical mechanics for students in engineering and the physical sciences. Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 1 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Rotational dynamics and angular momentum; equilibrium and elasticity; periodic motion including LRC electrical circuits; gravitation; fluid mechanics; temperature; thermal expansion; heat and the first law of thermodynamics; heat conduction; kinetic theory of gases; entropy and the second law; heat engines.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.

items.text: AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Mechanical waves, wave interference and normal modes, sound and hearing, electric field, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Vectors, velocity, acceleration. Newton's laws. Work and energy. Linear momentum. Gravity. Static equilibrium. Rotational motion. Angular momentum.

nodes.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Physics 6A.
nodes.description: Self directed laboratory course where students seek to discover simple mathematical descriptions of laws governing various physical phenomena. Each student is responsible for deciding what to measure, how to measure it, and what interpretation can be placed on the results.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 6A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Oscillatory motion. Vibrations, waves, sound. Fluids. Electrostatics and DC circuits. Magnetism and magnetic forces. Induction and Faraday's law. AC circuits. If time permits: Heat and thermodynamics.

nodes.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Physics 6B.
nodes.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 6B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Electromagnetic waves. Geometric optics, optical instruments. Interference and diffraction. Quantum theory of the atom. Nuclear physics. If time permits: Special relativity, elementary particle physics.

nodes.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Physics 6C.
nodes.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Physics Course Options
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Kinematics in 3D, Newton’s Laws, Energy, Momentum and Collisions, Rotation, Statics and Equilibrium
